data.title: Fix bug B870263cf90: ddflow_digest misses the help-group ratchet on main (Unmapped)

data.claim: ddflow_digest lands in the Unmapped group because grouped_tools claims a tool by a _GROUPS prefix, else by a declared help_group; ddflow_digest has neither. A one-line _GROUPS addition classifies it.
data.falsifier: grouped_tools(TOOLS) returns an Unmapped group containing ddflow_digest, and test_every_tool_is_in_a_help_group_and_a_tier asserts that set is empty.
data.mechanism: grouped_tools walks _GROUPS prefixes then declared help_groups, and files what neither claims under Unmapped.
data.probe_output: UNMAPPED GROUPS contains ddflow_digest; tier=all; placement=ddflow_view action=digest
data.question: Is ddflow_digest filed under Unmapped solely because _GROUPS has no digest prefix?

evidence.note: Empirically confirmed: group dict of grouped_tools(TOOLS) has {'Unmapped — add a prefix to _GROUPS': ['ddflow_digest']}; ddflow_digest tier=all, placement=ddflow_view/action=digest. Research R83d42636cc (CONFIRMED).

Governing rules hold: bug-fix task auto-filed with phase bugs and wave tag (r-task-phase-needs-wave); fix ships a regression test that fails against the unfixed guard (bug-closes-with-regression-test); README tool table regenerated alongside the code change (r-docs-with-the-change); gemini reviewer key will be loaded from the git-ignored secrets file before review (r-gemini-key-load).

chunk_findings.detail: The change adds a brand-new `("Reading the queue", ("waves", "digest"))` entry after `"When something is wrong"`. The bug description says only `digest` was missing a prefix and asks to add `"digest"` under the existing `"Reading the queue"` group, which already contains `"waves"`. This insertion therefore creates a duplicate `"Reading the queue"` group and a duplicate `"waves"` prefix. Consumers that iterate `_GROUPS` (for example `ddflow help` or README table generation) will now emit two "Reading the queue" sections, with `ddflow_waves` listed in both, while the new test uses `dict(grouped_tools(TOOLS))` and can hide the duplicate. The correct change is to add `"digest"` to the existing `"Reading the queue"` prefix tuple, not to insert a second group.

Empirically in the worktree, dict(grouped_tools(TOOLS)) returns EXACTLY ONE 'Reading the queue' group == ['ddflow_digest','ddflow_waves'] and UNMAPPED == {}. There is no pre-existing 'Reading the queue' _GROUPS tuple (it came only from ddflow_waves' help_group, now folded into the explicit prefix beside digest).
